messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT STREAM] spike in inference/latency-high — ~120 pages/min in last 5m, ~90% of active PagerDuty pages. Alert IDs: A-50321, A-50322
maria: saw it, is this customer-impacting? any 5xxs?
josh: no 5xxs, mostly tail p99 spikes on a subset of model hosts. retries/backpressure increasing. customers may notice slowness, not errors.
liam: taking lead — we need to limit PD fatigue. proposal: immediate 'rate-bucketing' + tag-based dedupe, then tune thresholds after traffic calms.
emily: +1. immediate mitigation idea: only page for severity=critical OR whitelisted prod-models; everything else -> #alerts slack.
maria: can we fingerprint by (model, region, host_pool) so duplicates collapse?
josh: yes — use alertmanager group_by on labels `model,region,host_pool`. then add rate-limiter per group (e.g., 1 page per 120s).
liam: action items (short):
- patch alertmanager route: group_by model,region,host_pool + rate_limit (liam)
- create temp PD suppression rule for low severity 20m (emily)
- add per-model p99 heatmap + page-count panels (maria)
- post-incident doc + tuning ticket (josh)
emily: creating temp suppression: `pdctl suppress create --service inference --scope low --duration 20m` :hourglass_flowing_sand:
maria: starting dashboard panel, will annotate incident window
josh: patch ready, testing on staging route. config snippet for prod router:
```
route:
  receiver: pagerduty-critical
  group_by: [ 'model', 'region', 'host_pool' ]
  routes:
    - match:
        severity: critical
      receiver: pagerduty-critical
    - match_re:
        severity: "(warning|info)"
      receiver: slack-alerts
      continue: false
  rate_limit:
    period: 120s
    bursts: 1
```
liam: timeline: suppression in ~5m, route change + group_by in ~15m, monitor for 1h, then reassess.
emily: also mapping PD escalation so only criticals escalate to oncall.
josh: once stable we'll draft an RFC for the 'rate-bucketing' pattern and add to runbook. filing ticket INFR-452 for follow-up.
maria: adding affected customers list to INFR-452 and linking dashboards
liam: handing off to night oncall; leaving checklist here. :white_check_mark:
incident-bot: suppression active (20m). pages reduced ~72% in first 3m. monitoring continues.
maria: confirmed pages down, dashboards show p99 still spiky for a few model shards but overall customer error rate unchanged.
liam: final notes for the ticket: look at p95 vs p99, consider separating noisy models into separate host pool or tune kernel IO for those hosts (long-term).
josh: thanks — scheduling post-incident sync tomorrow 10:00am and will move deeper analysis into INFR-452. closing live-mit thread, continue follow-up in ticket.
